### Q1. JEE Main 2026 (06 April Shift 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Difficulty Level:* `2`

The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with Br$_2$/KOH (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is :
<img style="width: 600px" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_april_watermarked/06APRS2__q68_d1.jpg" />

**Options:**

- **(A)** $5$
- **(B)** $4$
- **(C)** $3$
- **(D)** $6$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) $3$**

**Detailed Solution:**

The reaction of an amide with $\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}$ (alcoholic) is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction is specific to primary amides ($R-\text{CONH}_2$) and produces primary amines ($R-\text{NH}_2$) with one less carbon atom.

Among the given compounds, the primary amides are:
1. Benzamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2$)
2. 2-Phenylacetamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$)
3. Acetamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$)
4. Cyclohexanecarboxamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CONH}_2$)

The other two compounds (N-ethylcyclohexanecarboxamide and N-methylpivalamide) are secondary amides and do not undergo this reaction.

The primary amines formed from the degradation of the four primary amides are:
1. Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$)
2. Benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$)
3. Methylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$)
4. Cyclohexylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NH}_2$)

The Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of aliphatic primary amines. It cannot be used to prepare aromatic primary amines (like aniline) because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

Therefore, aniline cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. The remaining three amines (benzylamine, methylamine, and cyclohexylamine) are aliphatic primary amines and can be prepared by this method.

Thus, there are $3$ compounds that satisfy both conditions.

Answer: $3$

</details>

### Q2. JEE Main 2026 (22 January Shift 2)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Difficulty Level:* `2`

<img style="width:500px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_q_69_1.png"> 
 The final product $[\mathrm{B}]$ is :

**Options:**

- **(A)** <img style="width:200px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_o_69_1_1.png">
- **(B)** <img style="width:200px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_o_69_2_1.png">
- **(C)** <img style="width:200px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_o_69_3_1.png">
- **(D)** <img style="width:200px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_o_69_4_1.png">

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(D) <img style="width:200px;" src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main_2026_watermark_improved/22S2_o_69_4_1.png">**

**Detailed Solution:**

Cyclohexylmethylamine reacts with benzoyl chloride under basic conditions to form amide [A]:
cyclohexylmethyl benzoamide.
LiAlH₄ reduces the amide carbonyl to CH₂, converting the N-benzoyl group to a benzyl group.
The product [B] is a secondary amine formed by reduction:
cyclohexylmethyl-benzylamine ($C_6H_{11}-CH_2-NH-CH_2-C_6H_5$).
This structure contains secondary amine (N-H) with two carbon substituents: cyclohexylmethyl and benzyl groups.

</details>
